propositions: Passing a verifier resumption the prior attempt's search frontier as a data-shaped exclusion list within the untrusted context fence does not reduce re-search overlap relative to cache-seeded control resumptions.

On both large-ticket test cases, treatment arm (frontier-informed) showed higher re-search overlap rates (45.0% vs 25.0%, 80.0% vs 50.0%) than control arm, failing the predeclared >=30% reduction threshold.

The inert fence design renders frontier evidence signaling unable to suppress re-grounding of unproven criteria; the frontier block instead acts as a signpost, causing the model to re-read listed files immediately.

Cache-seeded resumption (locust behavior) already removes dominant redundancy from re-proving credited criteria; frontier exclusion lists cannot suppress the remaining re-grounding of still-unproven criteria at the evidence layer.
